title: Derived sections continuity for bounded-below systems on finite-cover sites
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty cofiltered category [def-weil-size-convention]. For every $i$ let $\mathcal C_i$ be a small site with finite limits and finite covering families, and for $a:j\to i$ let $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ be a morphism of sites induced by a finite-limit-preserving functor $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ taking covering families to covering families. Assume the identities and composition laws hold, and put $\mathcal C=\varinjlim_i\mathcal C_i$, $p_i:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]. Write $R\Gamma$ for total right derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sp-kinjective-bridge, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix an integer $b$. Let $K_i^\bullet$ be complexes of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C_i$ which are zero in degrees below $b$, and let $\alpha_a:f_a^{-1}K_i^\bullet\to K_j^\bullet$ be maps of complexes satisfying the identity and cocycle laws, using inverse image on abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Set $K^\bullet=\varinjlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}p_i^{-1}K_i^\bullet$, the termwise colimit of complexes of sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$\operatorname*{colim}^{\mathrm{der}}_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}R\Gamma(\mathcal C_i,K_i^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathcal C,K^\bullet).$$
Here the source is the exact filtered derived colimit: choose compatible bounded-below injective-resolution complexes for the system and take the termwise filtered colimit of their global-section complexes. The arrow is induced by the projection pullbacks followed by the actual coprojections to $K^\bullet$. The isomorphism is natural for maps of the coefficient systems, compatible finite-cover site functors between such systems, and cofinal reindexing. In particular its cohomology maps are the canonical filtered-colimit maps, and the same construction for every canonical truncation $\tau_{\le r}K_i^\bullet$ [def-kun-truncations] is compatible with the truncation inclusions and their maps to the untruncated complexes. No uniform bound on cohomological dimensions is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), using Tag 0EXZ (lemma-colim-sites-injective); bounded-below derived extension by the canonical truncation spectral sequence, derived.tex lemma-two-ss-complex-functor. This is the general finite-cover tool underlying ILO XX 4.4, printed p.373, passage from (**) to (**)lim.

proof.text: Regard $(K_i,\alpha_a)$ as the bounded-below complex $K_{\mathscr S}$ of the system category in [lem-per-varying-site-system-injective-resolutions]. Choose its monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $s:K_{\mathscr S}\to J_{\mathscr S}$ there, preserving the lower bound $b$. Evaluation gives compatible maps $s_i:K_i\to J_i$, with all $J_i^n$ injective. Thus $R\Gamma(\mathcal C_i,K_i)$ is represented by $\Gamma(\mathcal C_i,J_i)$, and the transition chain maps are the actual adjunction-unit section maps followed by the transitions of $J$. Their identity and composition laws hold because those of the system and of the adjunction units hold. These models therefore form an actual diagram of complexes, rather than an independently chosen family of resolutions.

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); system embedding construction: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0EXZ

proof.text: Put $L=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}J_i$ termwise, and let $t:K\to L$ be induced by the $s_i$. Exactness of every $p_i^{-1}$ and of filtered colimits of abelian sheaves shows that cohomology of these complexes commutes with these operations: kernels and images are preserved, so $H^n(t)=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}H^n(s_i)$ is an isomorphism. Thus $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $L^n=0$ for $n<b$. For every $q>0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites] to the sheaf system $(J_i^n)_i$ and a terminal object at any fixed stage. Finite-limit preservation makes its images terminal. Its stage cohomology groups vanish because $J_i^n$ is injective; hence $H^q(\mathcal C,L^n)=0$. Every term of $L$ is consequently global-section acyclic.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), applied to the terms of the compatible injective resolution; exactness as in its proof

proof.text: The degree-zero continuity theorem [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites-sections], applied to each $J_i^n$ at a stage terminal object, gives the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_i\Gamma(\mathcal C_i,J_i^n)\cong\Gamma(\mathcal C,L^n)$. To pass from the arrow category over a fixed $i_0$ to all indices, a cocone on the former extends to an index $j$ by choosing $k\to i_0$ and $k\to j$ and using the $k$-component. Two choices give the same map after a common refinement equalizing the relevant arrows; existence and independence follow from cofilteredness. This proves the colimit identification by the cocone universal property. The displayed degreewise maps commute with differentials: each is the section map of $J_i^n\to p_i^{-1}J_i^n\to L^n$, and these are chain maps. We obtain an isomorphism of complexes $A:=\varinjlim_i\Gamma(\mathcal C_i,J_i)\xrightarrow{e}\Gamma(\mathcal C,L)$.

source.place: Tag 09YN (sites.tex lemma-colimit), the degree-zero case used in Tag 09YP

proof.text: By exactness of filtered colimits in $\mathbf{Ab}$, termwise filtered colimit preserves quasi-isomorphisms: it preserves the kernel, image and quotient defining each $H^n$. Thus $Q A$ represents the exact filtered derived colimit in the statement. Let $\eta_L:Q\Gamma(L)\to R\Gamma(QL)$ be the derived-functor unit. By [sk-thm-acyclicity] it is invertible, since $L$ is bounded below and termwise acyclic. Therefore $R\Gamma(Qt)^{-1}\circ\eta_L\circ Qe$ is an isomorphism $Q A\to R\Gamma(QK)$ in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. This constructs the derived comparison itself; taking cohomology is a consequence.

source.place: Tag 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity), canonical comparison for a bounded-below acyclic complex

proof.text: We identify this arrow with the prescribed pullback/coprojection arrow. Resolve $K\to R$ on $\mathcal C$ by a bounded-below injective complex, chosen monomorphically. Since $t:K\to L$ is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] gives $v:L\to R$ extending $K\to R$. The $i$-th leg of $\Gamma(v)e$ is exactly $\Gamma(J_i)\to\Gamma(p_i^{-1}J_i)\to\Gamma(L)\to\Gamma(R)$. This is the resolution formula for pullback followed by the actual coprojection $p_i^{-1}K_i\to K$: the map $p_i^{-1}J_i\to R$ extends that coprojection after the augmentations. By the derived-unit naturality equation $R\Gamma(Qv)\eta_L=\eta_R Q\Gamma(v)$, its localization equals the arrow in Step 4. Consequently all its cohomology maps are the canonical filtered-colimit maps.

For a map $h$ of coefficient systems, choose monomorphic system resolutions $K\to J$ and $K'\to J'$. The lift theorem in the abelian system category gives $\widetilde h:J\to J'$ extending $h$. On sections the square of $e$ maps commutes termwise, since both composites are induced by the same coprojections and $\widetilde h_i$. Apply derived-unit naturality to the induced map of the $L$ complexes. This gives naturality of the comparison of Step 4. Two lifts are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]; applying additive inverse image, sections and termwise colimit preserves the homotopy equation. Taking $h=1$ and exchanging the two resolutions proves independence of all resolutions and the identity and composition laws.

For compatible site functors between two such diagrams, form the small combined index category with both copies of the original indices and the connecting site morphisms, imposing the given commuting-square relations. The two coefficient systems and their specified comparison form one system on this category. Apply [lem-per-varying-site-system-injective-resolutions] once on the combined category. Its restrictions have injective terms at every site and give STRICT commuting transition and connecting maps. They therefore compute both derived-colimit diagrams. The ordinary section maps commute with the maps $e$ because the adjunction units and the actual coprojections commute with the connecting morphisms. Apply the construction of Step 5 on the two limit sites: each resulting map into a receiving injective resolution extends the same coefficient/coprojection map, so homotopy uniqueness identifies it with the canonical site-pullback map. Thus the derived continuity square commutes. To compare these restricted models with system-injective models used earlier, lift their monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms into those system-injective models; Step 6 then gives the same derived square.

source.place: Tags 013P, 013S; sites-cohomology.tex Remark 08J6 (remark-before-Leray), adjunction-unit construction of cohomology pullback

proof.text: For cofinal_reindexing, take homology in each integer degree. Exactness of filtered colimits in abelian groups makes the homology functor preserve the section-diagram colimits. Objectwise quasi-isomorphisms therefore give an objectwise invertible natural transformation on homology; its colimit is invertible. The naturality equation colimit.post A H followed by H(colim.map v.sections) equals colim.map (whiskerRight v.sections H) followed by colimit.post B H. Both colimit.post maps are invertible, so cancellation proves colim.map v.sections is a quasi-isomorphism. The final-functor theorem makes the actual map colimit.pre N.sections.diagram U.index invertible. Their composite is v.sourceMap; localization makes it invertible. The previously stated naturality theorem supplies v.Commutes. This is a complete Lean proof and uses no boundedness beyond the given models. For each integer $r$, exact inverse image and exact filtered colimit commute with $\tau_{\le r}$: its only modified term is $\ker(d^r)$, with its induced differential and inclusion. Apply the coefficient-map naturality of Step 6 to every inclusion $\tau_{\le r}K_i\to K_i$ and $\tau_{\le r}K_i\to\tau_{\le s}K_i$ for $r\le s$. All these systems retain the lower bound $b$ (and are zero when $r<b$). This gives exactly the asserted truncation squares. Only bounded-below acyclic computation has been used, so no cohomological-dimension bound enters.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q139-f63952736 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item and its one new node are correct and well split; I made no changes. The item is not a 2026-10-21 re-split: Q49 created it on 2026-10-24 as an unsplit node with no proof. Its statement is word for word the base statement; only def-kun-truncations was added to stmt_deps, and that node does define tau<=r in any abelian category. It is a true derived form of Stacks 09YP for bounded-below complexes of abelian sheaves. The base change is pullback then coprojection, in the same coefficient category as 09YP and the pbc nodes. No duplicate exists: the etale-limit-complex-systems node covers schemes and H^p only, and cohomology-colimit-of-sites covers sheaves only. Sources read: sites-cohomology.tex 0EXZ (l.2855, the product of f_{b*}A_k), 09YP (l.2905), derived.tex 013K(3) (l.6280), and the tags 015E, 070J, 013P, 013S. Steps: (1) the system resolution makes each J_i K-injective by kinjective-computes(2), so RGamma(C_i,K_i) is Gamma(C_i,J_i) by def-sfb-right-derived-functor; the transitions are unit then system map, using terminal objects preserved by u_a. (2) Exact p_i^{-1} and filtered colimits make t a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism; cohomology-colimit-of-sites at a terminal X_{i0} plus vanishing on injectives makes L termwise acyclic; u_{i0}X_{i0} is terminal in C. (3) Degree-zero sections continuity, extended from the arrow category over i0 to all of I by cofinality, gives an isomorphism of complexes. (4) Filtered colimits in Ab are exact and sk-thm-acyclicity inverts the unit, giving the derived-form isomorphism. (5) Lift along the monomorphic quasi-isomorphism into a bounded-below injective R, then unit naturality, identifies it with the pullback/coprojection arrow; the pullback map for complexes is written out through resolutions rather than cited from a node, which I accept. (6) Lifting and homotopy uniqueness in the abelian system category give naturality and independence of resolutions. (7) One resolution on a combined index category gives strict squares, without assuming restriction keeps system-injectivity. (8) Initial-functor-limit handles cofinal reindexing, and tau<=r commutes with the exact functors. The new node lem-per-varying-site-system-injective-resolutions is true. The system category S is abelian with kernels and cokernels computed at each site because each f_a^{-1} is exact. Evaluation at k has a right adjoint built from products of pushforwards, which gives enough injectives as in 0EXZ but at the level of systems. Evaluation at i has an exact left adjoint built from sums of pullbacks, so it preserves injectives. 013K(3) applied in S gives the monomorphic resolutions. Edge cases checked: empty I, one object, loops in I, any bound b. B1-B9 hold (statement only, self-contained, definitions cited, three kinds of Mathlib search recorded). D1 holds: the node makes no continuity claim. Duplicate candidates were checked and differ (colimit-of-sites-injective-system, semisimplicial-ringed-total-category, complex-injective-resolution-mono). I accept the declared tool_uses: they are generic tools from sk-thm-p1, sk-thm-acyclicity, kinjective-computes and initial-functor-limit. No SGA source is used.
